data.narrative:
Quantum Art is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $140M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 11 comparable firms: 3 public companies (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum datapoint thresholds (fewer than 3 observations within narrow valuation tiers). The primary method employed is stage-progression analysis, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $140M raised proxy, reflecting typical valuation dynamics from Series A to the subsequent funding round. This method yields an implied valuation of $280M.

The triangulated analysis, based on the single applicable methodology, supports a valuation range of $238M (low) to $322M (high), with a median of $280M. The width of this band reflects uncertainty inherent in relying on a single method and the absence of narrow-peer calibration. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight comparables at Quantum Art's stage and the sensitivity of stage-progression estimates to assumed step-up multipliers. Broader market conditions in quantum computing and company-specific progress milestones will materially influence actual valuation outcomes.
